pages.actualObservation: Lecture60 title, author/institution/campus image, footer1. No substantive technical claim.
Six topic headings: application domains, ethics, safety, future, review, careers; footer2. No additional technical claim.

Footer3. Vision-guided assembly adapts grip/placement to part variation; predictive maintenance fuses sensors and ML to forecast failures/reduce unplanned downtime; AMRs use SLAM/path planning in dynamic warehouses. Empty outlined lower-right rectangle, not a plotted figure.

Footer4. CNN defect inspection; cobot force/torque sensing plus compliance; digital twins mirror production for pre-deployment optimization. Safety is an intended application benefit, not proof that any cobot is inherently safe; downstream safety pages qualify it. No equations/code; empty outlined rectangle.

Footer5. Surgical example names da Vinci and precise kinematics/real-time vision; rehabilitation exoskeletons/assistive arms use adaptive control; eldercare combines mobile robots and HRI for daily living/well-being. Brand example is not a claim of unsupervised surgery or a patient recommendation.

Footer6. Hospital medication/sample/supply delivery uses navigation; imaging AI assists radiologists; prosthetics combine EMG-driven interfaces and learned control policies. Read high-sensitivity phrase as intended role, not a universal measured score.

Footer7. Vision for crop health/weeds/ripeness enables targeted rather than blanket treatment; autonomous-vehicle example fuses sensing/planning/RL; UAV surveying/delivery/infrastructure combines GPS pathfinding and obstacle avoidance. Example techniques not mandatory for every vehicle.

Footer8. AUV SLAM localization for seabed/pipeline/environmental tasks; construction bricklaying/rebar/site surveying uses dynamics/trajectory generation; space arms/rovers use autonomy where communication delay precludes direct real-time teleoperation. High-level delayed supervision is not excluded.

Footer9. Domestic SLAM/obstacle avoidance; retail shelf/inventory vision and NLP assistance; conversational/HRI voice interaction; humanoids integrate perception/planning/dynamics/learning. General examples, not guaranteed features of every commercial device.

Footer10. Ethical questions beyond engineering correctness: degree of decision authority, reward versus human intent, designer/operator/owner accountability question, designed graceful degradation to human oversight. Liability is posed as an open question, not assigned legally.

Footer11. Training-data bias in CV/NLP; uneven face/speech performance across demographic groups; physical consequences; fairness testing within validation. No numeric dataset or preferred fairness metric provided.

Footer12. Pervasive camera/microphone/LiDAR collection; minimization of collection and retention; discard/anonymize unnecessary data; shared-space consent legal/ethical questions. Do not turn this into jurisdiction-specific legal advice or imply names alone anonymize data.

Footer13. Ownership posed among manufacturer/operator/observed people, not decided. Sensor/behavior records can expose daily-life patterns. Regulatory-gap claim and engineer ethical baseline are general course framing, not a statement that existing privacy laws do not apply.

Footer14. Repetitive manual/cognitive tasks, concentrated region/sector displacement, lagging retraining and unequal gain distribution contrasted with cobot augmentation, maintenance/supervision/design roles, dull/dirty/dangerous tasks and historical job creation. These trends do not guarantee each displaced worker gets a new role.

Footer15. Ethics as design requirements from day one; explicit adjustable autonomy, predeployment bias audit, documented collection/retention, explainable decision logs and affected stakeholders beyond customers.

Footer16. Real-time collision avoidance needs latency bounds in shared spaces; Cartesian force/velocity limiting; soft joints/backdrivable actuators complement software. Compliance is not a complete injury guarantee; source supplies no numerical injury threshold or certified stop bound.

Footer17. E-stop independent of AI software/hang; proximity zones slow then stop; redundant independent sensing limits one-sensor failure. Independence and diagnostic coverage are assumptions, not guaranteed by merely duplicating a sensor.

Footer18. RL out-of-distribution behavior, confidently wrong perception, sim-to-real dynamics mismatch, reduced interpretability versus PID/LQR. Opening contrast does not mean conventional control has no uncertainty or OOD failure.

Footer19. Classical safety-envelope override; confidence monitoring/conservative fallback; domain randomization; human override for high-consequence decisions. Confidence monitoring is not sufficient alone given preceding confidently-wrong warning. Domain randomization narrows, not proves zero gap.

Footer20. ISO10218 industrial arms/integration;ISO/TS15066 collaboration;ISO13482 personal care. No editions provided. Risk process: hazards over full envelope; severity/likelihood; simplified hierarchy eliminate/engineer/guard/warn-or-train; test before sign-off and after changes. Do not label this as a complete normative standard or certification procedure.

Footer21. Safety ongoing process: near-miss logging/review, training-distribution boundary tests, simple auditable safety code separated from learned complexity, simulation→constrained pilot→rollout with gates; mechanical/software/procedural independent layers.

Footer22. Foundation vision-language-action models aim cross-task generalization; multi-agent fleets learned communication/shared policies beyond centralized-only; soft/bio-inspired compliant materials plus learned control. These are stated research aims, not guaranteed universal capabilities.

Footer23. Domain randomization/differentiable simulation for transfer; active perception chooses movement/view for information; few-shot aims handful of demonstrations rather than thousands. No numerical sample bound, learning guarantee or live system result.

Footer24. Explicitly directional, not predictive trajectory: near-term cobots/AMRs and commoditized fusion/SLAM; mid-term general manipulation/minimal retraining; longer-term household/service humanoids conditional cost/safety/dexterity; norms/regulation alongside technology. Do not convert horizons into promised dates.

Footer25. Large-workspace cable-driven/novel mechanisms; wall-climbing infrastructure inspection; space dynamics+AI beyond real-time Earth control; robust perception in disaster/extreme conditions. Conditional communication/hazard argument, not prohibition of delayed supervision.

Footer26. Opportunity claims: lower sensor/compute costs, transfer learning data efficiency, cloud/edge capability-latency balance, open ROS frameworks reducing development cycles. These are course trends, not present price guarantees.

Footer27. Novel-environment generalization, brittle long-horizon plans, energy density/battery duration, trust/regulation/acceptance remain challenges. No battery specifications or quantified reliability supplied.

Footer28. Review explicitly assigns Weeks1–2 foundations/ROS/spatial/FK/IK/Jacobians, Week3 Newton–Euler/Lagrange/state-space dynamics, Week4 joint/Cartesian trajectories and mechanism design. Review only; check earlier-source links before deciding repeated disposition.

Footer29. Week5 linear/nonlinear/Cartesian control; Week6 ML/Python/trees/forests/Q-learning grasping; milestone modelling/control/initial learning. Review of previously taught methods, not a new algorithm.
Footer30. Week7 vision/image/features/ANN/YOLOv8; Week8 A*/grid/obstacle/deepRL/GPS/fuzzy; Week9 genetic paths/neural navigation/localization/SLAM. Review only, no new figures/code/equations.
Footer31. Week10 NLP/transformers/speech/conversation/HRI/emotion; Week11 hardware/sensors/actuators/armML/dynamics/integration; milestone complete sensing/navigation integration. Review only.

Footer32. Spatial/kinematic foundations across arm/mobile tasks; recurring Newton–Euler/Lagrange; state-space links classical control and RL; linear algebra/probability throughout ML/SLAM. Cross-topic connections, no new mathematical derivation.

Footer33. RL across grasping/path planning/navigation; vision into detection/SLAM/demonstrations; techniques tied to applications. Cross-domain transfer of learning framing, not proof identical learned policy transfers unchanged.

Footer34. Humanoid perception/HRI; industrial dynamics/trajectories; ROS connecting modules; mobile navigation autonomous behavior. Wording calls demonstrations proof that every module composes; qualify as illustrative integration, not formal proof of universal correctness or hardware replication.

Footer35. Robotics engineer integrates systems with kinematics/dynamics/control; AI/ML builds perception/decision models; perception specialist vision/SLAM. Roles overlap; ask source-listed primary focus rather than exclusive job boundaries/current vacancy claims.
Footer36. Embedded/hardware sensors/actuators/compute; controls feedback design; test/safety behavior and compliance validation. No salary or hiring outcome data.

Footer 37. Graduate MTech/PhD specialization in cable-driven, soft, multi-agent or learning control; research assistants in university/industry labs; publishing venues ICRA/IROS/RSS and Indian AIR/iNaCoMM. Paths, not current openings or admission guarantees.

Footer 38. National/corporate R&D including ISRO/DRDO applies research to missions; interdisciplinary biology, materials and cognitive science; postdoctoral path toward academia, not mandatory or guaranteed faculty appointment.

Footer 39. Service/inspection opportunities in agriculture, logistics and infrastructure; component sensors/actuators/AI modules supplied to integrators; general expanded funding claim, not verified current grants or guaranteed business success.

Footer 40. Portfolio from personal/course/open-source work; ROS/simulation contributions; competitions test engineering constraints; networking via IEEE-RAS, local meetups and conference student programs. Attributed lecture guidance, not new external commitments.

Footer 41. Continuous deliberate learning via conference abstracts/talks (ICRA/IROS/CoRL), ROS2/simulation/open datasets, revisiting foundational mathematics/dynamics/control, and communities. No code, equations or measured outcomes.
